Subject: Split-pool reserved + burst credits proposal and perf/$ tradeoffs

Hi Alice + Carlos,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate you walking through CloudWave's 90-day launch profile. Based on the usage sample you shared, I sketched a pragmatic packaging approach that addresses predictable steady-state throughput while capping cost during unpredictable spikes: a split-pool model. High level:

- Base reserved pool: commit to a steady baseline sized in A100 80GB (good perf/$ for mid-length inference) that covers 70-80% of your daily token volume.
- Burst pool: a smaller, on-demand H100-backed burst pool for priority latency-sensitive surges and batch backfills; paired with pre-purchased "surge credits" so you don't pay retail burst rates during product launches.
- Memory tilt option: for very large-context jobs we can offer L40S nodes for a small portion of the reserved pool to avoid OOMs without inflating the entire commit.

Ask: can you confirm the 99th percentile latency requirement for customer-facing calls (is 120ms P99 acceptable), and the percentage of requests that must be served from the lowest-latency tier? That will determine how much we keep in the H100 burst pool vs the A100 reserve.

Attached is a simple worksheet where you can drop your daily token/seq-length distribution (cloudwave_usage_profile_may2028.csv) — if you send that back I will run a perf/$ sizing and a recommended commit + surge-credit ladder.

Pricing note (ballpark): we typically recommend sizing the base commit to the 60-75% steady-state for best perf/$ and covering spikes with either pre-bought surge credits (discounted) or a small on-demand burst pool. Discount elasticity: larger 12-month commits unlock steeper discounts on both reserved unit price and surge-credit unit price.

Next steps: if you want, Ben (cc'd) can run an internal perf matrix for your sample and Markus can sketch discount tiers. Happy to set a 30-min follow up after we get the usage CSV.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — attached our anonymized 30-day trace (see cloudwave_usage_profile_may2028.csv). A few clarifications up front:

- P99 requirement: for the public-facing chat flow we'd like <= 120ms P99 for text-gen at 2k tokens. For async backfills the slowness is OK.
- Memory: about 4% of calls require >20k context and currently blow past 80GB when we keep full history; for those we prefer a cheaper path than forcing H100 for all traffic.
- Cost target: we need perf/$ that beats our current in-house A100 fleet by ~15% after discount to justify migration.

Questions:
1) Can you show perf/$ for A100 80GB vs H100 80GB vs L40S (48GB) at avg seq lengths: 512, 2k, 10k?
2) How do surge credits price vs on-demand bursts (what discount do you typically grant on pre-purchased credits)?
3) If we size the base commit conservatively (60% steady-state), what is the expected overage exposure in a 95th-percentile traffic day?

Thanks — if you can send the perf matrix and a straw-man pricing ladder that maps commit size -> unit price -> surge-credit discount, we can review with finance.

Best,

Subject: Re: Split-pool reserved + burst credits proposal and perf/$ tradeoffs

Team — ran the benchmarks and sketched a pricing ladder. High-level summary first, numbers attached in redwood_perf_matrix_may2028.pdf.

Benchmarks (inference throughput, tokens/sec, normalized perf/$):
- A100-80GB: seq512 -> 9.5k t/s (best perf/$ on short-medium seq); seq2k -> 3.2k t/s; seq10k -> 420 t/s
- H100-80GB: seq512 -> 12.8k t/s; seq2k -> 4.6k t/s; seq10k -> 680 t/s (H100 moves the needle for latency-sensitive 2k and long-context work)
- L40S-48GB: seq512 -> 7.8k t/s; seq2k -> 2.4k t/s; seq10k -> 540 t/s (L40S pairs well for high-memory long-context at lower cost than H100)

Perf/$ (relative to our baseline internal price unit):
- For seq512: A100 best, H100 ~+20% perf but perf/$ ~+8% worse; L40S ~-10% perf vs A100 but similar perf/$ for long-context when you avoid multi-splitting.
- For seq2k: H100 becomes competitive: H100 perf/$ ~+6% vs A100.
- For seq10k: L40S often beats A100 perf/$ because it avoids memory-thrashing even if raw tokens/sec lower than H100.

Commit + surge-credit ladder (12-month):
- Base commit tiers (monthly equivalent shown):
  * Small: 8 A100 units (recommended for PoC) — unit price X_small
  * Mid: 24 A100 units (recommended steady-state) — unit price X_mid (~18% discount vs retail)
  * Large: 64 A100 units — unit price X_large (~30% discount)
- Burst / surge credits:
  * On-demand bursts: retail pricing (no discount)
  * Pre-purchased small pack (10% discount on burst unit price) — intended to cover minor campaigns
  * Pre-purchased large pack (25-35% discount depending on commit size) — for predictable launch windows

Overage exposure at 60% base commit: our simulator says median overage days ~7-9% additional spend, 95th-percentile days can be 30-45% more if they have a multi-day launch; that is where pre-buys help cap marginal cost.

Recommendation:
- Base commit: A100-80 for ~65% steady-state.
- Reserve 2-4 L40S nodes within the same pool for long-context jobs to avoid routing everything to H100.
- Buy a moderate large surge-credit pack (25% discount) sized to cover one medium campaign per quarter.

I've attached the perf matrix and an example cost calculator (redwood_perf_matrix_may2028.pdf). Markus — if you can confirm the max approved discount band for pre-buys we can finalize the ladder for Alice.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alice / Carlos —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the perf matrix + a straw-man commercial proposal summarized below:

- Base commit (12-mo): 24 A100-80 units (covers ~65% steady state) at unit price X_mid (approx 18% off retail).
- Long-context safety: 3 L40S-48 units reserved in the same pool (small tilt) to serve the ~4% >20k context calls.
- Burst handling: H100-backed on-demand burst pool available; we recommend purchasing a quarterly surge-credit pack equal to ~20% of expected monthly burst consumption (25% discount on surge-credit unit price).
- P99 target: with 24 A100 + 3 L40S + 1-2 H100 hot nodes for low-latency routing we project P99 ~110-120ms at 2k tokens for the public flow.
- Expected overage exposure if base set to 60%: ~10% median extra spend; capped to ~3-8% marginal increase if the surge-credit pack is used during launches.

If that looks good I can generate a mutual action plan and a DocuSign package for signatures. Proposed next steps:
1) Your finance signs off on the tiers and discount bands — we can flex the surge-credit discount a bit if they move the base commit up to 36 units.
2) Legal/Procurement: we'll send standard SOW + SLA addendum.
3) Kickoff: delivery team will run a smoke benchmark against your prod trace and finalize routing policies.
